value_or_angle: old="How can you reach me?" header="How are you connected to the founders?" body="I'm a Northern Californian because of two migrations: my father's side came west in 1851, when Charles Hooker and two of his brothers left New England and he started a hardware business in San Francisco, and my mother's mother came in the 1950s, to get a divorce in Reno and start over there. I always assumed the Hooker line ran through my father and the Talcott line through my mother, then learned that my mother descends from Thomas Hooker too. All told, I'm connected to 22 of Hartford's original founders through 27 direct lines, three of them to John Stanley and two to Stephen Hart." category=family

value_or_angle: old="Why build this project?" header="Why build this project?" body="I grew up hearing that my family went far back in American history, but no one could tell me exactly how. My great-grandfather was Samuel F. B. Morse, and I assumed he descended from the inventor of the telegraph; he was actually a distant cousin, named in the inventor's honor. I also took credit all through high school for General Joseph Hooker, until I learned he had no children, and that left me needing to find out more." category=family
